text: Git is a version control system that helps developers track changes in their code. One of its most useful features is branching. A branch lets you work on new ideas without affecting the main code. Developers often create feature branches to build a new function safely. When the work is finished, they merge the branch back into the main project. Before merging, teams usually open a pull request so others can review the changes. This workflow keeps the project stable and organized. By using branches, merges, and pull requests, teams can collaborate smoothly and avoid mistakes in their shared code.
